calls.video_title: Tesla Is Investing Aggressively in its Next Generation Technology | TSLA Stock Analysis
calls.stance_flip: Parkevtate was HOLD on TSLA (his own stated prior stance - upgraded from SELL at $300 earlier in 2026, not in tracked calls.json), now SELL at ~$379
calls.price_at_call: trading at $379 (stated); his DCF fair value $113/share (stated), ~70% downside over 12-18 months; forward P/E 175 (stated)
calls.thesis: SELL - first tracked Parkevtate TSLA call (only prior tracked entry was UNCERTAIN on 4 Oct). He states in the video he is downgrading Tesla back to a selling opportunity today (22 Oct in-video date): he had it as a SELL for most of 2026, upgraded to HOLD when it fell to $300 (where he closed his puts/short for a profit), and now at ~$380 he is tempted to buy put options again, more so near $400.
calls.base_case: Q3: revenue flat at $28bn YoY, EPS down 44%, auto revenue down 3% to $20.5bn, energy revenue down 16%, operating margin down from 5.8% and operating income down 56%; he raised near-term DCF estimates only because 2026 capex was cut from $25bn to $20bn.
calls.bull_case: FSD subscriptions up 67% to 1.74m at ~$99/month (high-margin recurring revenue), services/other revenue up to $4.6bn, Tesla Semi volume production started, and four new European FSD approvals (Croatia, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Slovakia); ~1,000 robotaxis testing in Austin.
calls.bear_case: Valuation prices robotaxis/robots as inevitable: 175x forward earnings is ~6x the S&P 500, ~40x the average carmaker and ~6x big-cap AI names. Chinese EV competition is eroding share in every contested region, EV volumes likely peaked near 2m a year, and any investor realisation that timelines slip could mean ~70% downside.

calls.video_title: Nvidia Just Gave Away the Next Boom (THIS IS HUGE!)
calls.price_at_call: about 200x next year's earnings (stated); no share price stated
calls.thesis: HOLD, first tracked BWB TSLA call (no flip) — his ladder has Tesla at 'fairly valued', but the reading rests only on outside estimates, and he takes Elon Musk's claims at about 10% of face value.
calls.base_case: About 1.7 million people pay for Full Self-Driving and for the first time half are on the $99-a-month plan — the one edge asset already collecting monthly revenue; latest-quarter spending on factories and computing roughly doubled year over year.
calls.bull_case: If humanoid robots and robotaxis scale even on the realistic path (Goldman Sachs: about 1m robotaxis worldwide by 2030, 6m by 2035; Bank of America: about 1.2m humanoids a year by 2030), Tesla is betting hardest on the winning category.
calls.bear_case: Musk's goal of 10 million robots a year is over eight times Bank of America's whole-market 2030 forecast; only about 25,000 humanoids shipped worldwide in the first half of 2026 and about 740 robotaxis were registered in Texas by mid-October versus the 1m promised for 2020; whales have been leaving for three quarters.

calls.thesis: AVOID — first tracked Joseph TSLA call, no prior stance, no flip: 'not interested in the company' and the Roadster demo 'doesn't convince me to buy the stock' — he cannot buy stocks just because they are cool when the future is already priced in; prefers SpaceX as the more unique, defensible, less competitive Musk investment.
calls.base_case: More of the same: a heavily narrative-driven quarter with little focus on fundamentals.
calls.bear_case: 154x forward P/E on revenue flat for ~2 years, deliveries down, net income down sharply and free cash flow flat; robotaxi rollout is slower, more methodical and more red-tape-bound than promised, against Waymo (~500k rides/week), Uber's multi-brand network and strong Chinese AV rivals.
